newsitem.title: USA: Two USDA officials tapped for top food slots.
newsitem.headline: Two USDA officials tapped for top food slots.

text.p: The Clinton Administration Tuesday tapped two Agriculture Department officials for top slots at the department overseeing food safety and public feeding programmes.

Arkansan Shirley Watkins was nominated to be USDA Undersecretary for Food, Nutrition and Consumer Services, in charge of the food stamp programme, school lunches and the popular Women and Infants Feeding Programme. Watkins had been deputy to the previous undersecretary, Ellen Haas.

Catherine Woteki, who holds a top job in the department's research arm, was appointed to the key post of Undersecretary for Food Safety, responsible for shepherding the department's programme to modernise federal meat inspection after 90 years.
Senate Agriculture Committee chairman Richard Lugar promised a prompt hearing and vote on the nominees. Dates for confirmation hearings probably will be set after Memorial Day, an aide said.
"I have just pled that somebody be sent," Lugar, Indiana Republican, told reporters, lamenting that it took so long for the administration to identify potential appointees.
"I think we need to have a full staff at USDA to get the job done. Certainly, Secretary (Dan) Glickman shares this view but these vacancies remain," he added.

Wotecki and Watkins would fill posts that have been vacant for months. Also open are two other undersecretary posts, one assistant secretary post and the top slot at the Farm Service Agency, which runs the farm programme.
